definition: The shared catalogues every style draws from and none owns: the element slots, the volumes a house can take, and the room types. A style does not own a cornice; it specifies one.
basis: Editorial, from VISION.md's first layer: "Element slots, volumetric massings, and room types. Three catalogues that every style draws from and none owns.", and its thesis: "The test of the ontology is that adding a style should never require adding a slot". docs/inheritance.md: "Georgian does not own a cornice — it specifies one."
